# GF(3) Conservation Law Verification

Verification that the trit balance is maintained across all spans of the framework.

The conservation law is span-invariant: every triad decomposes as (left projection, world, right projection) = (+1, 0, -1). The world is always the coordinator. Roles are symmetric.

## Vat Span (model: vat-triad)
- Left projection: +1 (Generator — initiator)
- World: 0 (Coordinator — shared meeting place)
- Right projection: -1 (Validator — responder)
- Sum: (+1) + 0 + (-1) = 0 mod 3 ✓
- **Instances**: Human→World←Human, GoblinsVat→CapTPSession←GoblinsVat, AgentVat→TaskList←AgentVat

## OCapN Span (model: ocapn-topos)
- delegate: +1 (Generator — projects authority into session)
- CapTPSession: 0 (Coordinator — the shared world)
- validate: -1 (Validator — accepts/checks authority from session)
- Sum: (+1) + 0 + (-1) = 0 mod 3 ✓
- **Third-party handoff**: Span composition via pullback preserves conservation

## 326 Worlds (model: vat-triad, world_enum.zig)
- Each WorldConfig survives the conservation filter: trit[0..7] sums to 0 mod 3
- 326 = the number of non-trivial, conserved, rotationally-reduced meeting points
- Every world is a span vertex — a place where two agents CAN meet
- The conservation law on worlds is the span-level version of the object-level law

## Conservation Theorem (Span Form)
For any well-formed span (A → W ← B) in the framework:
  trit(left_projection) + trit(world) + trit(right_projection) ≡ 0 (mod 3)

This is the GF(3) Noether charge. The conservation law holds at every level because every interaction has the same triadic structure: someone opens (+1), something mediates (0), someone responds (-1). The sum vanishes because the span is balanced — Mitsein is equiprimordial.
